chunks.content: 96 The Problem with “Passive Income” Plumbing Companies Hi Sara, If you’ve been on YouTube in the last six months, you’ve probably seen it: another glossy video telling you that buying a “boring” business (think HVAC, plumbing, car washes) is your ticket to sipping champagne on a yacht while your new company runs itself. Let’s burst that bubble—gently, but thoroughly. Spoiler alert: there’s nothing “passive” about clogged toilets and broken soap dispensers. Here’s the Not-So-Boring Truth: These businesses aren’t bad buys—in fact, they can be excellent ones—but they are people-heavy, compliance-laden, and deeply operational. You want to run a car wash? Fantastic. Just know that someone’s going to have to restock soap, clean up after messy customers, and handle complaints from people convinced your very expensive machinery scratched their 2002 Honda Civic. You want to buy an HVAC business with zero experience in HVAC? I love your optimism. But unless you’re a professional management company with a team ready to run the business for you, prepare for a crash course in employee drama, regulatory headaches, and insurance chaos. Here’s Why People Sell These “Cash Cows”: Because they’re tired. Because they’ve been in the trenches dealing with payroll, collections, broken equipment, and burnt-out technicians. Buying one of these businesses isn’t a walk in the park—it’s a full sprint through a people-powered obstacle course. So, Should You Buy One? Maybe! If you’ve got the grit, the systems, and the support, it can be a profitable ride. But here’s an insider tip: accounting practices are flying under the radar right now. They’ve got: Great margins (sometimes 30-40%!) Clean books (literally their job) Less red tape (particularly if you’re buying a non-attest firm) We’ve got more on this at Deal Academy, where we walk you through how to spot the right opportunities and avoid the common pitfalls that turn dream deals into disasters. Want to learn how to buy a business without buying a headache? Check out our courses and stay tuned—we’re doing a deep dive soon on how to evaluate and acquire accounting firms the smart way.
